entries.title: Bourgeois Dignity
author: McCloskey, Deirdre N.
entries.credentialing: University of Chicago Press monograph; author is an emeritus professor of economics and history with a substantial peer-reviewed publication record.
entries.notes: Argues the Great Enrichment is explained by a shift in attitudes toward commerce rather than by capital accumulation or exploitation. Heterodox on interpretation, unimpeachable on standing — the archetypal tier 2 entry.

entries.title: The WEIRDest People in the World
author: Henrich, Joseph
entries.credentialing: Author chairs the Department of Human Evolutionary Biology at Harvard; the book's core arguments derive from peer-reviewed work in psychology and anthropology.

entries.title: Laws of the Game (Football Association)
author: Football Association
Morley, Ebenezer Cobb
entries.notes: Adopted 8 December 1863; thirteen laws. Public domain. Explicit modelling on MCC cricket codification. This is the published-rules claim itself, not a description of it. Tier 1 primary text for the rationalization / rule-bound contest argument under Science ↔ Sports.

entries.title: Liber de Spectaculis (conventional title)
author: Martial
entries.notes: Contemporaneous source for the Colosseum inaugural games (80 CE). Public domain. Title Liber de Spectaculis is post-classical (Gruter); recent editors prefer Liber Epigrammaton. Epigram 1: all labor yields to the Caesarean amphitheatre. Epigram 29 (Titus freeing gladiators after equal contest) usable for governing-rule argument — but concede the volume also celebrates lethal venationes and executions. Ker Loeb (1919) is public domain; Shackleton Bailey Loeb is in copyright. URL confirmed live 2026-08-25.

entries.title: From Ritual to Record: The Nature of Modern Sports
author: Guttmann, Allen
entries.credentialing: Columbia University Press monograph; author was Professor of American Studies at Amherst College with a substantial peer-reviewed record in sport history.
entries.notes: Spine source for Science ↔ Sports. Seven characteristics of modern sport. First published 1978; cite the 2004 revised edition (contains Guttmann’s own retrospective critique). Page locators are edition-specific. Load-bearing for the discontinuity thesis.

entries.title: The Olympic Myth of Greek Amateur Athletics
author: Young, David C.
entries.credentialing: Monograph by a classicist; reviewed in Journal of Hellenic Studies 106 (1986). Author held academic posts in classics.
entries.notes: Demonstrates that ancient Greek ‘amateurism’ is a modern myth constructed by the Olympic movement. Closes the continuity-via-amateur-ideal route. Must be read before any page that touches Greek athletics.

entries.title: Games and Empires: Modern Sports and Cultural Imperialism
author: Guttmann, Allen
entries.credentialing: Columbia University Press monograph; same author standing as From Ritual to Record.
entries.notes: Imperial-diffusion critique of modern sport’s global spread. Cite it yourself before a critic does.

entries.title: Spectacles of Death in Ancient Rome
author: Kyle, Donald G.
entries.credentialing: Routledge academic monograph; author is a specialist in ancient sport and spectacle with a peer-reviewed publication record.
entries.notes: Precise treatment of lethality in the Roman arena (executions, venationes, gladiatorial combat). Use to keep the Roman side factually tight — avoid the flattened ‘slave death matches’ phrasing. ISBN confirmed via Journal of Roman Archaeology review.

entries.title: The Lure of the Arena: Social Psychology and the Crowd at the Roman Games
author: Fagan, Garrett G.
entries.credentialing: Cambridge University Press monograph; author held an academic post in classics/ancient history.
entries.notes: Social psychology of the Roman crowd and arena. Complements Kyle. Paperback ISBN 978-0-521-18596-7; confirm hardback if a single canonical identifier is required. Reviewers expected a range of responses to the application of modern social psychology to Roman crowds.

entries.title: The Roman Amphitheatre: From Its Origins to the Colosseum
author: Welch, K.
entries.credentialing: Cambridge University Press monograph; author is a specialist in Roman architecture and archaeology.
entries.notes: Direct Architecture-root match for the September Colosseum / amphitheatre material. Strongest scholarly source currently identified for the building itself. Author given as K. Welch pending verification of full given name.
